note: Both sets mix sound spec/finish claims with speculative bindings of bare dimension strings to named objects, but Set A is the stronger extraction: it keeps the full clearance note's second condition (1\" either side), correctly binds the bulkhead cladding/finish and the 3/4\" MDF gable, and repeats itself far less. Set B states the same 3/4\"=1'-0\" scale three times and the same 1/2\" MDF finish and 3'-0\" island height under two or three names, and it invents three DINING TABLE properties (overhang 6\", clearance height 3'-0\", thickness 5\") plus conditions the page never states. Set A's weaknesses are an invented condition (\"dimension B\") and a few loose bindings (MWK04 width 2 ft, DINING TABLE height, DIRTT wall width 4'-0\"); Set B does capture the 2\"x6\" framing size and the 12\" clear-above that Set A omits.
remarks: Text layer is a jumble of isolated dimension strings and tags with no positional binding, so several dimension-to-entity assignments (5\" as backsplash vs. table thickness, 4'-0\" as wall vs. platform width, 2'-0\", 8\", 3'-0\" near DW/MWK04) cannot be confirmed at this image resolution; I treated unverifiable bindings as unsupported rather than as confirmed errors where the value itself is real. Both sets miss the larger overall dimensions on the sheet (6'-7 1/2\", 3'-3 3/4\" x2, 8'-4\" in A only via B, 2'-2 3/16\", 2'-5 1/16\", 7'-0 1/8\", 6 1/2\") and the 2\"x6\" FRAMING / 1/2\" MDF bulkhead build-up is split inconsistently between them. Recurring pattern: extractions turn bare dimension strings into confident object attributes and then fabricate conditions to make them read plausibly.
